title: Downsizing in Denver: Tips for a Smooth Transition
excerpt: Downsizing can be a difficult task… but not with these tips!
author: Kevin B
content:
At some point, many homeowners decide it’s time to downsize. Often, this happens when children move out, leaving behind extra bedrooms, unused space, and more upkeep than necessary. Suddenly, a smaller home feels like the smarter and easier choice.

If you're considering downsizing in Denver, here are a few simple ways to make the process smoother.

Declutter First

Before moving, take time to let go of what you no longer need.

Old furniture, storage boxes, and sentimental items can quickly make a smaller home feel crowded. Ask yourself what truly serves a purpose in your next space.

Less clutter means more comfort.

Ask for Help

Sorting through years of belongings can be overwhelming.

Ask family members or close friends to help you decide what stays and what goes. They may also want to keep meaningful family items, helping you preserve memories without keeping everything.

Plan Ahead

Downsizing takes time.

From garage sales and donations to storage planning and preparing your current home for sale, starting early helps reduce stress and makes the move much easier.

Know What You Want

Everyone downsizes for a reason - think about what matters most in your next home.

Do you want fewer stairs? Less maintenance? No yard work? Better walkability? Defining your priorities helps you find the right fit.

Looking to downsize? We’ve got condo and townhome properties that fit every lifestyle.

See our new home listings

Use Smart Storage Solutions

Multi-purpose furniture like storage ottomans, beds with drawers, and expandable tables can help maximize a smaller space while keeping your home functional and organized.

Expect an Adjustment Period

Moving to a smaller home is a lifestyle change.

There are many benefits - less cleaning, lower costs, and simpler living but it may take time to adjust. Give yourself grace during the transition

🌿 How to Keep Your House Cool Without AC

Energy-Efficient Cooling Tips to Reduce Your Summer Energy Bills

When summer temperatures rise in Colorado, many homeowners rely heavily on air conditioning to stay comfortable. But running your AC all day can quickly lead to high energy bills and unnecessary energy use.

The good news? You can keep your house cool without AC by using smart, energy-efficient strategies that work with your home not against it.

Below are practical, proven energy-efficient cooling tips to help you stay comfortable while lowering your summer energy bills.

☀️ Block Heat to Keep Your House Cool Naturally

One of the most effective ways to cool your home naturally is to stop heat before it enters.

Best strategies:

  • Close blinds or curtains during peak sunlight hours
  • Use blackout or thermal curtains for insulation
  • Add exterior shading like awnings, overhangs, or trees

Windows are responsible for most indoor heat gain. Blocking sunlight is a key step in passive cooling strategies for homes.

🌬️ Use Cross-Ventilation for Natural Cooling

If you want to keep your house cool without AC, airflow is essential.

How to improve air circulation at home:

  • Open windows early morning and late evening
  • Create cross-ventilation by opening windows on opposite sides
  • Use fans to move cool air in and hot air out

Pro tip:
Close windows during the hottest part of the day to trap cooler air inside.

🪟 Upgrade to Energy-Efficient Windows (or Improve Existing Ones)

Windows play a major role in energy-efficient home cooling.

Benefits of energy-efficient windows:

  • Reflect heat instead of absorbing it
  • Reduce indoor temperature fluctuations
  • Lower reliance on air conditioning

If replacing windows isn’t an option:

  • Install reflective window film
  • Use cellular shades to improve insulation

🧊 Use Fans Correctly to Stay Cool

Many people misunderstand how fans work.

Fans don’t lower room temperature they help cool your body, making you feel more comfortable.

How to use fans efficiently:

  • Set ceiling fans to rotate counterclockwise in summer
  • Turn fans off when you leave the room
  • Combine fans with open windows at night for better airflow

This is one of the simplest low-cost ways to reduce summer energy bills.

🌿 Use Landscaping for Passive Cooling

Your outdoor space can directly impact your indoor comfort.

Sustainable cooling tips:

  • Plant trees to shade windows and walls
  • Use xeriscaping and drought-tolerant landscaping
  • Add greenery near your home to reduce heat absorption

These passive cooling techniques are especially effective in dry climates like Denver.

⚡ Reduce Indoor Heat to Keep Your Home Cool

Appliances and lighting can add unnecessary heat inside your home.

Easy ways to reduce indoor heat:

  • Avoid using ovens during the hottest part of the day
  • Switch to LED bulbs (they produce less heat)
  • Run appliances like dishwashers at night

These habits support energy-efficient living and help maintain a cooler home.

Insulation for Year-Round Energy Efficiency

Insulation isn’t just for winter it’s essential for keeping your house cool in summer too.

A well-insulated home:

  • Prevents heat from entering
  • Keeps cool air inside longer
  • Reduces the need for constant AC use

This is a key feature of energy-efficient homes and high-performance construction.

💡 Why Energy-Efficient Cooling Matters

With rising temperatures and energy costs, more homeowners are searching for ways to:

  • keep their house cool without AC
  • lower monthly utility bills
  • live more sustainably

The solution isn’t just using less energy it’s using smarter home cooling strategies designed for efficiency.

🌞 Final Thoughts: Cool Your Home Smarter This Summer

You don’t need to rely entirely on air conditioning to stay comfortable.

By using a mix of:

  • passive cooling techniques
  • improved airflow
  • energy-efficient upgrades

you can cool your home naturally, reduce your summer energy bills, and create a healthier living environment.

Spring Home Refresh Tips for Denver Homeowners: Create a Healthier, Energy-Efficient Home

Spring in Denver brings warmer temperatures, longer days, and the perfect opportunity to refresh your home. After months of colder weather, many homeowners are ready to open their windows, bring in fresh air, and make small upgrades that improve comfort and energy efficiency.

For Denver homeowners, spring is also a great time to focus on healthy living, indoor air quality, and sustainable home improvements. These small seasonal updates can help reduce energy costs, improve home wellness, and create a more comfortable environment year-round.

Here are seven spring home refresh tips designed specifically for Denver homes and Colorado’s unique climate.

1. Replace HVAC Filters for Better Indoor Air Quality in Denver Homes

One of the easiest ways to improve your home’s air quality is by replacing your HVAC filters.

During winter, dust and allergens accumulate in heating systems. Changing filters in the spring helps remove pollutants and prepares your system for warmer weather.

Benefits of replacing HVAC filters:

  • Improves indoor air quality

  • Reduces allergens and dust

  • Improves HVAC efficiency

  • Helps lower energy bills

Denver’s dry climate can increase airborne dust, making regular filter replacement especially important.

2. Maximize Natural Light in Your Denver Home

Denver enjoys more than 300 days of sunshine each year, making natural light one of the city’s best lifestyle advantages.

Maximizing natural daylight can reduce energy use and improve mood and productivity.

Ways to increase natural light in your home:

  • Clean interior and exterior windows

  • Replace heavy winter curtains with lighter fabrics

  • Rearrange furniture to allow more sunlight

  • Use mirrors to reflect natural light

Homes designed with large windows and open layouts often use sunlight as a natural energy source.

3. Add Indoor Plants for Healthier Living

Houseplants are a simple way to improve the atmosphere inside your home. Many plants help create a calming space while supporting a healthier indoor environment.

Popular low-maintenance houseplants include:

  • Snake plant

  • Pothos

  • Peace lily

  • Rubber plant

Adding greenery is a growing trend in home wellness design and sustainable interior living.

4. Upgrade to Energy-Efficient Lighting

Switching to LED lighting is one of the easiest ways to improve energy efficiency.

Compared to traditional bulbs, LED lights:

  • Use up to 75% less energy

  • Last significantly longer

  • Produce less heat

  • Lower electricity costs

Many Denver homeowners are now combining LED lighting with smart home systems to optimize energy use.

5. Refresh Outdoor Living Spaces

Outdoor living is a major part of the Denver lifestyle. As spring arrives, patios, balconies, and rooftop decks become extensions of indoor living spaces.

Consider refreshing your outdoor area with:

  • Weather-resistant furniture

  • Native Colorado plants

  • Solar lighting or string lights

  • Container gardens

Creating functional outdoor areas can increase both home enjoyment and property value.

6. Improve Water Efficiency with Sustainable Home Upgrades

Water conservation is an important part of sustainable living in Colorado.

Spring is a great time to check for leaks and upgrade water fixtures.

Simple improvements include:

  • Installing low-flow showerheads

  • Fixing leaking faucets

  • Upgrading irrigation systems

  • Using drought-resistant landscaping

These upgrades reduce water waste while lowering monthly utility costs.

7. Consider a Healthier, Energy-Efficient Home Design

Many modern homes in Denver are being built with energy efficiency, sustainability, and indoor health in mind.

Features commonly found in eco-friendly homes include:

  • Energy-efficient windows and insulation

  • Improved ventilation systems

  • Sustainable building materials

  • Smart energy management technology

These homes not only reduce environmental impact but also create healthier indoor environments for homeowners.

Why Healthy Homes Matter in Denver

Denver homeowners are increasingly prioritizing homes designed for wellness, sustainability, and energy efficiency.

A healthier home can:

  • Improve indoor air quality

  • Reduce energy costs

  • Increase comfort year-round

  • Support long-term sustainability goals

With Colorado’s focus on environmental responsibility, sustainable home design continues to grow in popularity across the Denver real estate market.

Frequently Asked Questions

What spring maintenance should Denver homeowners do first?

Start with HVAC filter replacement, checking for leaks, cleaning windows, and preparing outdoor living spaces for warmer weather.

How can I improve indoor air quality in Denver?

Replace HVAC filters regularly, improve ventilation, add indoor plants, and reduce dust buildup caused by Colorado’s dry climate.

Are LED lights worth it for homeowners?

Yes - LED bulbs use significantly less energy, last longer, and reduce monthly electricity costs.

content:
Sustainable Holiday Decorating: Eco-Friendly Ideas for Your Home

The holidays bring sparkle and joy—but they can also bring excess waste. Between disposable decor, over-the-top lighting, and single-use wrapping, it’s easy for sustainability to get lost in the festive spirit. Fortunately, sustainable holiday decorating makes it possible to celebrate beautifully while caring for the planet. Sustainable holiday decorating involves using natural, upcycled, or reusable materials—like pinecones and evergreen branches—choosing biodegradable or recycled ornaments, switching to energy-efficient LED lighting, and even opting for live or potted Christmas trees. By prioritizing minimalist designs with one or two focal points, you can reduce clutter while creating an elegant, eco-friendly atmosphere. And when the season ends, natural materials can be composted, while other decorations can be reused, recycled, or donated.

Sustainable Decorating Ideas

1. Utilize Nature

Bring the outdoors in with natural elements such as pinecones, evergreen branches, and dried leaves collected from your yard or local park. Use them to craft wreaths, garlands, and table centerpieces that feel timeless and organic. When the season’s over, these materials can be composted, keeping your decorations waste-free. 👉 Tip: Add dried orange slices or cinnamon sticks for a fragrant, festive touch.

2. Repurpose and Upcycle

Give old decorations new life. Repaint worn ornaments or turn scrap materials—like cardboard, old magazines, or fabric remnants—into handmade holiday treasures. You can even craft ornaments from dried fruit slices or recycled paper, making each piece both sustainable and meaningful.

3. Embrace Biodegradable Options

Skip the plastic and choose decorations made from biodegradable materials such as paper snowflakes, corn husk ornaments, or natural twine. For sparkle, try biodegradable glitter instead of the traditional microplastic kind—it’s just as festive and far more earth-friendly.

4. Choose Reusable Decor

Invest in durable, reusable pieces that can last for years, like fabric garlands, wooden ornaments, and metal wreath frames. Proper storage helps these items look new year after year—saving both money and resources.

5. Select Sustainable Trees

When it comes to Christmas trees, consider alternatives that go beyond the cut-and-toss model. Choose a live tree that can be planted after the holidays, a potted tree that can return each season, or even a rented tree from a local farm. For a creative twist, decorate a large houseplant as your festive focal point. 🔗 Learn more: Tips for Choosing a Sustainable Tree

6. Use Energy-Efficient Lighting

Traditional incandescent lights use a lot of power—and burn out quickly. Switch to LED, rechargeable, or solar-powered lights, which use up to 80% less energy and last much longer. Use timers or smart plugs to automatically turn them off overnight. 🔗 Explore: Energy-Efficient LED Holiday Lights

7. Go Minimalist

Less is more when it comes to eco-conscious decorating. Create one or two striking focal points—like a beautifully decorated mantle or a centerpiece of natural greenery—and resist the urge to overfill every surface. Minimalist designs not only reduce waste but also create a calm, intentional aesthetic.

Post-Holiday Practices

When the celebrations are over, sustainability doesn’t have to stop.
  • Compost Natural Materials: Evergreen branches, pinecones, and other organic decor can go straight into your compost pile.
  • Reuse or Recycle: Pack away reusable decorations for next year, and look for local recycling programs for items that can’t be saved.
  • Donate or Give Away: If you’re simplifying, donate gently used decorations to friends, family, or local charities to extend their life and reduce waste.
Sustainable holiday decorating is about mindful celebration—choosing materials and traditions that align with your values and protect the environment. Whether it’s through reusable decor, biodegradable materials, or minimalist design, small choices can make a big impact. This holiday season, let your home shine with warmth, creativity, and care for the planet. MORE INFORMATION

title: How to Winterize a Sustainable Home: Green Tips for November & December

author: Kevin B
content:
How to Winterize a Sustainable Home: Green Tips for November & December

Winter in Colorado can be beautiful—but it can also mean higher energy bills if your home isn’t prepared. Winterizing your home sustainably not only keeps you cozy but also reduces your environmental footprint. Here’s how to get your green home ready for November and December.

1. Upgrade Your Insulation

Proper insulation is the foundation of a sustainable winter-ready home. Look for eco-friendly options like recycled insulation or sheep’s wool insulation, which help reduce energy consumption while minimizing environmental impact. Focus on:

  • Attics and basements

  • Exterior walls

  • Crawl spaces

Learn more about eco-friendly insulation options that improve energy efficiency.

2. Seal Leaks and Drafts

Air leaks are one of the biggest culprits behind rising energy costs. A few sustainable fixes include:

  • Eco-friendly weatherstripping for doors and windows

  • Caulking gaps around windows, doors, and vents

  • Checking seals around chimneys and fireplaces

These small changes can make a big difference in your home’s comfort and energy footprint.

3. Harness Passive Solar Heating

Take advantage of the sun’s natural warmth with passive solar strategies:

  • Keep south-facing windows clean and unobstructed

  • Open curtains during sunny winter days to warm interiors naturally

  • Close curtains at night to retain heat

Passive solar design is a simple way to reduce heating energy without extra technology or costs.

4. Optimize Heating with a Smart Thermostat

A smart thermostat allows you to efficiently manage your home’s temperature, saving both energy and money. Set lower temperatures when you’re away and program gradual heating for when you return. Popular options include Nest Thermostat or Ecobee.

5. Choose Sustainable Materials

When making winter upgrades, prioritize sustainable materials:

  • Recycled or natural insulation

  • Eco-friendly weatherstripping

  • Low-VOC paints and sealants for indoor air quality

These choices keep your home warm, healthy, and environmentally responsible.

Winterizing a home doesn’t have to compromise sustainability. By upgrading insulation, sealing leaks, leveraging passive solar heat, and using smart thermostats, you can create a cozy, energy-efficient home this November and December. Small, green steps today can lead to big energy savings and a more comfortable home all winter long.

For more sustainable home tips and Colorado real estate insights, visit redT Homes Blog.

Buying a Home Before the New Year: Why November Is the Time

As the year draws to a close, the real estate market presents unique opportunities for buyers. November, often overlooked, can be an ideal time to purchase a home. Here's why:

🏡 1. Less Competition

With the holiday season approaching, many potential buyers pause their home searches. This means fewer buyers in the market, allowing serious buyers to negotiate better deals without facing bidding wars.

💸 2. Motivated Sellers

Sellers listing their homes in November are often eager to close before the year ends. Whether due to job relocations, financial considerations, or the desire to finalize a sale before the holidays, these sellers may be more willing to negotiate on price and terms.

📊 3. Year-End Tax Benefits

Closing on a home before December 31st can offer significant tax advantages. Buyers may be eligible for deductions on mortgage interest, property taxes, and closing costs, potentially reducing their taxable income for the current year.

📉 4. Lock in Current Interest Rates

Interest rates can fluctuate, and while they remain favorable, purchasing a home now allows buyers to lock in current rates. Even a slight increase in rates can significantly impact monthly payments, so acting sooner rather than later can be financially advantageous.

🛠️ 5. Assess Home Performance in Colder Months

Buying in November allows buyers to evaluate a home's performance during colder weather. It's an opportunity to check heating systems, insulation, and overall comfort, ensuring the home meets expectations during winter months.

🎁 6. Move In Before the Holidays

Closing before the end of the year enables buyers to settle into their new homes before holiday festivities begin. This timing can reduce stress and allow for a smoother transition into the new year. Ready to stop renting and start building your future?

  • Grow Wealth Through Real Estate – Homeownership has always been one of the most reliable ways to build wealth. Rent-to-Own makes that possible now, without waiting on the “perfect” market.

A Smarter Path to Homeownership

The old stigma around Rent-to-Own is gone. Today, it’s a tool for first-time homebuyers, move-up buyers, and anyone who wants to be strategic in a competitive housing market.

If you’re waiting for the “right time” to buy, Rent-to-Own gives you a way to:

Fill Your Home with Natural Fall Scents

  • Orange peels 🍊

  • A few cinnamon sticks

  • Whole cloves

  • Star anise

Within minutes, your home will be filled with a warm, inviting scent — all without harsh chemicals.

🎃 DIY Organic Pumpkin Spice Mix

Pumpkin spice doesn’t just belong in lattes. Whip up your own organic blend to use in baking, oatmeal, or even sprinkled on roasted squash. Here’s a simple recipe:

  • 3 tbsp ground organic cinnamon

  • 2 tsp ground organic ginger

  • 2 tsp ground organic nutmeg

  • 1 tsp ground organic allspice

  • 1 tsp ground organic cloves

Mix and store in a sealed glass jar. This little spice jar is autumn magic — add it to coffee, warm milk, or baked goods for instant fall flavor.

Fall is the season of layering. Add warm throws, textured pillows, and earth-toned decor to your living room or bedroom. For a sustainable touch, consider choosing organic cotton or recycled fabric options — better for the planet and your home.

Denver’s fall can swing from sunny, warm afternoons to chilly nights, so maintaining energy efficiency is key. Here’s how:

  • Seal Windows and Doors: Check for drafts and gaps around windows and doors. Caulking and weatherstripping can prevent heat from escaping.

  • Check Heating Systems: Schedule a professional inspection of your furnace or heat pump. Replace filters for optimal performance.

  • Use Smart Thermostats: Program your thermostat for Denver’s fluctuating temperatures. Smart controls can save energy while keeping your home cozy.

At redT Homes, all our residences are designed with energy-efficient construction, including high-performance insulation and ENERGY STAR® appliances, helping homeowners save on utility bills year-round.

2. Maintain Your Fireplace for Safe, Warm Evenings

Nothing says fall like curling up by a fire. Make sure your fireplace is ready for use:

  • Clean the Chimney: Remove soot and debris to prevent blockages or fire hazards.

  • Inspect for Damage: Check for cracks or wear in the fireplace and flue.

  • Test Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Detectors: Ensure safety systems are functional before regular use.

Many redT Homes feature modern, high-efficiency fireplaces that not only provide warmth but are designed with sustainable heating in mind, minimizing environmental impact while maximizing comfort.

3. Insulate for Cooler Nights

Denver’s fall evenings can get chilly, so proper insulation is crucial:

  • Check Attics and Basements: Ensure insulation is intact to reduce heat loss.

  • Seal Gaps Around Plumbing and Vents: Prevent cold drafts from sneaking into your living spaces.

  • Use Thermal Curtains: Heavy, insulated curtains can keep heat inside and reduce energy usage.

redT Homes incorporate high-quality insulation and building materials as standard, creating a comfortable indoor environment that reduces energy waste and keeps you warm even on the coldest nights.

4. Prepare Your Landscaping for Fall

Even your yard benefits from seasonal prep:

  • Rake Leaves and Mulch Plants: Protect root systems from frost and prevent pests.

  • Winterize Outdoor Faucets: Shut off exterior water and drain hoses to prevent freezing.

  • Plant Native, Low-Maintenance Plants: Denver’s fall is ideal for planting species that thrive in seasonal conditions.

redT Homes communities often integrate eco-friendly landscaping principles, including drought-tolerant plants and low-maintenance yards, making seasonal upkeep easier and more sustainable.

5. Enjoy Fall Comfort with Less Stress

By taking these steps, you can enjoy Denver’s beautiful fall season without worrying about drafts, energy waste, or chilly nights. Sustainable features in redT Homes—like energy-efficient appliances, superior insulation, and eco-conscious materials—make seasonal transitions smoother, comfortable, and good for the planet.

Pro Tip: Fall is also a great time to inspect home systems, upgrade insulation, and plan any energy-efficient renovations before winter. Your home—and the environment—will thank you.

Fall in Denver is magical, and preparing your home properly ensures you can enjoy every colorful moment. With redT Homes, sustainability and comfort go hand in hand, making seasonal prep easier and more effective. Whether it’s maximizing energy efficiency, maintaining your fireplace, or insulating against cold nights, your home can stay cozy, eco-friendly, and beautiful all season long.

author: Kevin B
content:
The 10 Most Walkable Neighborhoods in Denver 2025

Whether you’re ditching the car, downsizing your commute, or just love the idea of grabbing coffee, groceries, and tacos without ever starting your engine, Denver has no shortage of neighborhoods where walkability rules.

In this guide, we’re breaking down the 10 most walkable neighborhoods in Denver for 2025, based on local amenities, transit access, and that hard-to-define vibe that makes a place feel effortlessly livable.

What Makes a Neighborhood Walkable? 

A neighborhood isn’t just walkable because it has sidewalks. The best walkable communities have:

  • A mix of uses (housing, retail, restaurants, parks)

  • Transit connections to downtown or nearby hubs

  • A safe, people-friendly design

  • A vibe that makes you want to explore

And in Denver, they tend to come with breweries. Lots of breweries.

1. Capitol Hill; One of the Most Walkable Neighborhoods in Denver

Walk Score: 93
Cap Hill is the OG of Denver walkability. Think historic mansions turned apartments, dive bars next to vegan cafés, and live music every night of the week. From grocery stores to bookstores, everything’s a short stroll away.

Local Favorite: Cheesman Park sunsets and late-night eats at City O’ City.

2. LoDo: Best Downtown Denver Neighborhood for Walkability

Walk Score: 91
LoDo combines old Denver charm with modern urban energy. Historic warehouses now house rooftop bars, and Union Station is your portal to the airport, mountains, and beyond.

Local Favorite: Brunch at Snooze, Rockies games at Coors Field.

3. Highland (LoHi)

Walk Score: 88
Trendy and ever-evolving, LoHi is full of boutiques, rooftop patios, and walkable bridges into downtown. It’s urban living with a neighborhood soul.

Local Favorite: Happy hour at Avanti + skyline views from the pedestrian bridge.

4. Five Points / RiNo

Walk Score: 87
Street art, breweries, music, and old Denver soul. This neighborhood blends rich history with serious edge—and it’s super walkable. Expect lofts, light rail stops, and a lot of art.

Local Favorite: Morning coffee at Crema, murals on every corner.

5. Baker

Walk Score: 86
Eclectic and energetic, Baker is full of vintage shops, dive bars, and renovated bungalows. South Broadway is your walkable spine—lined with record stores, pho spots, and indie theaters.

Local Favorite: First Fridays on Santa Fe and a nightcap at Historians Ale House.

6. Congress Park

Walk Score: 84
Quiet, leafy streets just a stone’s throw from Cherry Creek and City Park. Congress Park blends classic Denver homes with walkable eats, libraries, and neighborhood bakeries.

Local Favorite: Pizza at Pizzeria Locale and movie nights at the Esquire.

7. Uptown

Walk Score: 83
Small but mighty, Uptown is packed with brunch spots, bars, and boutique apartments. It borders City Park and offers easy walkability to downtown and medical campuses.

Local Favorite: Outdoor seating at Ace Eat Serve and walks through Benedict Fountain Park.

8. Speer / Alamo Placita

Walk Score: 82
A hidden gem just south of downtown, Speer offers walkable living with a relaxed vibe. The Cherry Creek Trail runs right through it, connecting you to nature and city life.

Local Favorite: Farmers markets and patios along 6th Ave.

9. Wash Park (West Washington Park)

Walk Score: 81
Known for its iconic park, this neighborhood isn’t just for runners and dog walkers—it’s also full of cozy cafés, bookstores, and restaurants worth the stroll.

Local Favorite: Morning coffee at Wash Perk before a lap around the lake.

10. City Park West: Quiet Walkable Living Near Denver’s Top Attractions

Walk Score: 80
Quietly one of the best places for car-free living, City Park West offers walkability without the downtown intensity. Bonus: walkable access to City Park, the Denver Zoo, and Museum of Nature & Science.

Local Favorite: Brunch at Olive & Finch and strolls through the park.

🧭 Final Thoughts

Denver’s walkable neighborhoods offer more than just convenience—they’re hubs of culture, community, and connection. Whether you’re buying your first condo, relocating from out of state, or just ready to swap traffic for tacos, these 10 neighborhoods prove you can live the Denver dream—one step at a time.

Small daily changes that lead to a healthier you — and a healthier planet. Sustainable living in 2025 is all about progress, not perfection. You don’t need to overhaul your home to make an impact. These five simple habits will help you reduce waste, improve indoor air quality, and create a more mindful space to live, work, and thrive.

Ditch the Harsh Chemicals

Swap traditional cleaning products for natural or non-toxic options. Not only are they safer for your health, but they also help reduce air pollution inside your home.

Let Fresh Air In

Opening your windows daily (even briefly!) clears out indoor pollutants and moisture. Fresh air = fresher perspective and better wellbeing.

Unplug When Not in Use

Devices like TVs and chargers continue to draw power even when turned off. Use smart plugs or power strips to cut phantom energy and save on electricity.

Use What You Have First

Before buying something new, see if you can repair, repurpose, or borrow instead. It’s a powerful way to reduce waste and shop more intentionally.

From reusable containers to refillable cleaning products, small plastic swaps add up. Start with the kitchen and work your way through the house. Want to live in a home that’s built for better living?

✅ Right-Sizing: Find the Space That Fits Your Life

There comes a time when the home you once needed becomes more than you really use. Whether your kids have flown the nest, your lifestyle has shifted, or you're just craving simplicity—you might be ready to right-size. Right-sizing isn’t about sacrificing space. It’s about finding the right space. A home that fits your current lifestyle, not your past one. So how do you transition gracefully into a space that feels just right? Let’s walk through it.

Start with What Matters Most

When you begin the right-sizing process, it helps to shift your mindset. Instead of thinking about what you're giving up, think about what you're making room for—less stress, more time, lower maintenance, and a space that works for how you live now. Ask yourself:
  • What spaces do I actually use every day?
  • What brings me joy (and what just collects dust)?
  • What would a simpler, more intentional space look like for me?

Edit Before You Move

Before you even start house hunting, give your current home a good once-over. That storage room you haven’t opened in a year? The formal dining set that only sees the light of day on Thanksgiving? It might be time to let go. Make three piles: keep, donate, and let someone else love it. Still struggling? Ask a trusted friend or family member to help you make those tough calls. Often, it takes a second set of eyes to remind you that you’re not parting with memories—just with the clutter.  

Look for Lifestyle Perks, Not Just Square Footage

Right-sizing doesn’t always mean going smaller—it means being smarter. The right home could be:
  • A modern townhome with zero yard work
  • A sleek condo in a walkable neighborhood
  • A cozy unit in a community with amenities you’ll actually use
Maybe you want a place with no stairs. Maybe you’re ready to trade your snow shovel for underground parking and a latte around the corner. Either way, your next home should make life easier—not more complicated.

Be Honest About the Adjustment Period

Change takes time. Even when it’s the right move, there’s a transition. Going from a larger home to a more manageable space might feel odd at first—but with a little patience (and a good furniture layout), you'll start to see the upside. You’ll clean less. Spend less. Worry less. And have more energy for the things you actually love.

Design for Dual Use

Right-sizing doesn’t mean doing without—it means doing more with your space. Look for multipurpose furniture:
  • Storage ottomans
  • Beds with built-in drawers
  • Dining tables that double as workspaces
Smart design can turn even a small space into something functional and beautiful.

Ready to Right-Size Without Compromise?

🧳 The Ultimate Moving Checklist: 10 Steps to a Smooth Move

Make your next move stress-free with this step-by-step guide! From packing hacks to utility setup, here’s everything you need to know for a smooth transition into your new home. So, you’ve just purchased a beautiful new home with redT—congratulations! Whether it’s a custom-built modern home or a move-in-ready new construction, this is an exciting next chapter. And while the hardest part of the buying journey might be behind you, the transition into your new space deserves just as much planning. To help you feel confident and organized, we’ve created the ultimate moving checklist—designed to make your move as smooth as possible.

1. Create a Moving Timeline (6–8 Weeks Out)

Start by setting your move-in date and working backward. Use a digital calendar or printable checklist to map out key tasks like hiring movers, scheduling utility transfers, and notifying your current landlord (if applicable). Pro Tip: If you're moving during peak season (late spring to summer), book movers early—they fill up fast!

2. Declutter Before You Pack

Now’s the time to lighten the load. Go through each room and donate, recycle, or toss what you no longer need. You’ll save time, space, and money on moving supplies. Bonus Tip: Use donation services like Goodwill or Pickup Please for easy pickups.

3. Get Quotes from Movers or Rental Trucks

Compare at least 3 moving companies or rental truck providers. Look at reviews, insurance options, and availability. Need a place to start? Check out:
  • Two Men and a Truck
  • U-Haul
  • Bellhop Moving
Hiring Movers? Ask about services like packing, unpacking, and large-item handling.

4. Start Packing Early

Begin with items you use less frequently—seasonal clothing, décor, books, etc. Label every box with the room name and a quick inventory. Color-coded tape or stickers can speed up unloading later. Packing Hack: Keep essentials like toiletries, chargers, and a change of clothes in a "first night" box. Looking for supplies? Try The Home Depot Moving Center

5. Set Up or Transfer Utilities

About two weeks before your move, contact utility providers to transfer or set up:
  • Electricity
  • Gas
  • Water
  • Internet & Cable
  • Trash/Recycling
If you're moving to Denver, check providers like:
  • Denver Water
  • Comcast/Xfinity

6. Change Your Address

Update your address with the USPS and notify banks, credit cards, insurance providers, and any subscription services. Don’t forget your employer and voter registration! 👉 Change your address with USPS

7. Plan for Pets & Kids

Keep little ones (and fur babies) safe and calm during moving day chaos. Arrange a babysitter or pet sitter, or set up a quiet room with snacks, toys, and comfort items. Bonus Tip: Look for local pet boarding options like Camp Bow Wow or trusted sitters on Rover.

8. Take Care of Your Current Home

If you're leaving a rental, clean thoroughly to ensure your deposit return. If selling, consider a professional clean before handing over keys. Extra Tip: Take final meter readings and photos to document the home’s condition. Services like Handy can connect you with local cleaners and handymen.

9. Do a Final Walkthrough

Before you lock the door one last time, check every closet, drawer, and cabinet. Make sure nothing’s left behind—and that everything’s packed securely. Optional: Snap a few final photos for your own memories or documentation.

10. Celebrate Your New Home!

Once you're in, unpack essentials first: kitchen, bedding, and bathroom supplies. Then take a breath, pop some bubbly, and enjoy your new space. Need help settling in? Your redT Homes agent can connect you with trusted local vendors for everything from landscaping to energy-efficient upgrades.

title: redT Homes Files Complaint Against Xcel Energy, Citing Over $18M in Losses and Nearly 5,000 Days of Project Delays
excerpt: redT Homes Files Complaint Against Xcel Energy, Citing Over $18M in Losses and Nearly 5,000 Days of Project Delays Denver, CO – July 1, 2025 – redT Homes, one of Colorado’s largest sustainable…
author: Kevin B
content:
redT Homes Files Complaint Against Xcel Energy, Citing Over $18M in Losses and Nearly 5,000 Days of Project Delays

Denver, CO – July 1, 2025 – redT Homes, one of Colorado’s largest sustainable housing developers, has filed a formal complaint with the Colorado Public Utilities Commission (PUC), calling for an investigation into Xcel Energy’s handling of new residential service requests. The complaint details 4,943 days of cumulative project delays, more than $18 million in direct losses, and the foreclosure of at least one development due to what redT calls “chronic inefficiencies” and “internal errors” at Xcel Energy. “After years of trying to resolve these issues directly with Xcel, including meetings with their executive leadership, we are left with no choice but to seek state intervention,” said Nathan Adams, redT’s CEO. “Xcel’s repeated design mistakes, last-minute changes, and lack of transparency have crippled our ability to deliver urgently needed, all-electric, LEED Gold-certified homes in Colorado.” The company’s June 18 letter to the PUC outlines: • Thousands of lost days across active housing projects • Uncompensated redesign and construction costs • Foreclosure due to power delays • Ongoing risk to company survival • Lack of meaningful accountability from Xcel In the letter, Adams urges the PUC to launch a formal investigation and implement new accountability measures for utility service timelines. “This isn’t just a redT issue—this is a housing issue,” Adams said. “Colorado’s housing shortage cannot be solved if its sole power provider continues to delay critical infrastructure without consequences.” A summary of the complaint and a detailed breakdown of project impacts is included in the public filing. Over the past 11 years, redT has built communities that prioritize sustainability, health, and long-term value for Colorado residents.

title: 🌿 The Benefits of Rooftop Decks, Gardens & Terraces for Urban Living and Wellness 🏙️
excerpt: 🌿 The Benefits of Rooftop Decks, Gardens & Terraces for Urban Living and Wellness 🏙️ City dwellers often crave natural spaces—but backyard access is rare in dense urban settings. Rooftop…
author: Kevin B
content:
🌿 The Benefits of Rooftop Decks, Gardens & Terraces for Urban Living and Wellness 🏙️

City dwellers often crave natural spaces—but backyard access is rare in dense urban settings. Rooftop decks and rooftop gardens can transform that limitation into an opportunity. Whether you’re looking for rooftop deck ideas, planning rooftop deck construction, or simply exploring urban outdoor living, here’s how they can enhance your life:

1. Create Valuable Outdoor Space

Expand your living area upward Rooftop decks extend usable square footage without sacrificing precious ground-level space—ideal for rooftop patio design dedicated to grilling, lounging, or play areas in the city. Privacy and panoramic views Elevated vantage points provide less crowded outdoor enjoyment and can deliver stunning vistas over the cityscape. If you’re searching for backyard alternatives, a rooftop terrace can be a perfect solution.

2. Boost Mental & Physical Health

Sunlight, fresh air, vitamin D Regular exposure to daylight and nature improves mood, concentration, and brain function. Incorporating biophilic design elements in your outdoor wellness space creates an oasis above the city. Stress relief through green design Adding greenery, like vegetated rooftops and potted plants, delivers serenity and supports mental health benefits of nature, lowering stress and enhancing emotional well-being. Physical activity encouraged Rooftop spaces make outdoor workouts, yoga, and gardening accessible, supporting healthier lifestyles. Whether you envision a rooftop garden or a minimalist deck, you can easily create a wellness space tailored to your needs.

3. Environmental Perks

Cools your home and city Green roof benefits include reduced heat gain, mitigation of urban heat islands, and lower cooling costs—an excellent example of sustainable building design. Improves air quality & stormwater control Plants filter pollution and absorb rainfall, easing runoff and refreshing your surroundings. Adding eco-friendly outdoor spaces also supports biodiversity in the city.

4. Enhance Property Value

Adds 5–25% to resale value Homeowners see an average return of 5–8%—and potentially 10–25% in upscale markets—thanks to extra usable space and rooftop deck aesthetic appeal. If you’re looking to add value to your home, investing in a rooftop terrace is a smart choice. Sustainable appeal & longevity Rooftop deck construction protects structural membranes, extends roof life, and may qualify for green building incentives that increase your property’s marketability.

5. Build Community & Connection

Social space for gatherings Shared rooftop patios become hubs for family, friends, and neighbors to connect, host barbecues, or hold community events. If you live in a condo or apartment, a rooftop terrace can serve as your communal backyard. Educational and communal gardening Rooftop gardens enable workshops, urban farming, and social bonding through shared green projects—key elements of urban outdoor living that strengthen community connections.

Design & Implementation Tips

  • Assess structural suitability: Anytime you add soil, furnishings, plants, or hot tubs, confirm load capacity and zoning codes before beginning rooftop deck construction.
  • Integrate biophilic design: Include greenery, water features, natural materials, and weather protection for full outdoor wellness benefits.
  • Choose low-maintenance selections: Opt for drought-tolerant plants, composite decking, or modular pavers to simplify upkeep and reduce rooftop deck cost.
  • Plan for different uses: Whether it’s sunbathing, dining, fitness, or peaceful retreats, design zones to match your lifestyle and create an inviting rooftop patio design.

Final Thought

Rooftop decks, terraces, and gardens are more than architectural features—they’re elevated sanctuaries that enrich urban living. They offer tangible benefits for well-being, the environment, and home value improvements. With thoughtful design and safety checks, you can transform unused rooftops into vibrant extensions of your home and community.

Better for You, Better for the Planet

Sustainable materials reduce waste, conserve natural resources, and lower greenhouse gas emissions during manufacturing and construction. By choosing eco-friendly options, redT Homes helps protect Colorado’s natural beauty—and ensures future generations can enjoy it too.
